messages:

To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearwavehealth.com
Date: 2029-10-15T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: High p99 latency + 503 token errors since 09:00 PT — impacting production

Rachel —

We're seeing a severe elevation in p95/p99 latency starting ~09:00 PT and a growing number of 503 token errors from the Redwood API. Throughput appears capped despite normal request volume; token-generation timeouts are surfacing in our service and causing request retries to pile up. This is affecting two critical customer workflows (claims ingestion + realtime triage) — we're getting customer complaints.

Attached are a set of samples (latency CSV + a screenshot of 503s). Can your team confirm whether this is a configuration/prefetch issue or something at the platform level? We had recent config changes to our priority lanes but did not touch cache settings.

We need an initial triage update in 30 minutes and a mitigation plan within 2 hours. Please escalate to engineering/ops as needed; our SLA is at risk.

Aisha
Director, Platform Engineering
Clearwave Health

Attachments: clearwave-latency-samples-1015.csv (text/csv), screenshot-error-503.png (image/png)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-15T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + 503 token errors since 09:00 PT — impacting production

Hi Aisha — thank you for the samples and the note. We're on it. Initial read: metrics and the pattern in the CSV look consistent with KV cache thrashing on the priority lane combined with HOL blocking from long-running generation requests. Two quick confirmations that will speed triage:

- Did you change the request distribution to send longer-context requests into your priority lane in the last 24 hours?
- Can you grant our ops team a short read-only log window (we'll share a narrow time range) so we can correlate token-reject traces?

Immediate mitigations we will try now (we'll report back within 20 minutes):
- Temporarily demote non-critical priority keys (ttl bump / move to standard lane) to free slots in the priority KV store.
- Reduce batch size on priority lanes to lower HOL blocking likelihood.
- Force-enable short-term prefix caching for repeated keys for 30m to stabilize hit rate.

Marissa and Ben from runtime are looped — Marissa will own the cache tuning and Ben will check routing and lane capacity. If this doesn't recover within 40 minutes we'll prepare an exec-facing summary and a customer credit ask.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: High p99 latency + 503 token errors — initial ops actions

Forwarding the thread and initial runbook notes. I spun a hotfix to reduce max_batch_tokens for the priority lane and bumped the per-tenant TTL for repeated keys to 30m as a short-term hedge. Observed behavior so far (first 10m after change):

- Priority lane hit-rate increased from ~27% -> ~62% (good)
- p95 dropped ~22% on the sampled endpoints
- 503 token errors decreased but still present at low volume

Outstanding: we still see occasional head-of-line stalls when very long-context requests (~6k tokens) land behind short inference tasks; this suggests per-worker batch locking is still causing HOL blocking. Proposed next steps:

1) Temporarily activate per-tenant soft prefetch (non-blocking) for the most common prefixes to reduce KV fetch latency variance.
2) For the next 2 hours, route long-context requests for Clearwave to a separate long-tail worker pool (isolates HOL blocking).
3) Post-mortem: check whether tenant's recent routing config change increased collision probability for priority slots.

I've started INF-1429 in Jira to track the follow-ups; assigning Ben for routing play and Jonas for capacity adjustments. Rachel, if you want an exec-ready note I can draft a short summary for leadership.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec brief requested: Clearwave instability, mitigation, and recommended customer relief

Team —

Summary (tl;dr): Clearwave Health experienced elevated p95/p99 latency and 503 token errors on 2029-10-15 starting at 09:00 PT. Root cause (probable): priority-lane KV cache thrash combined with HOL blocking from interleaved long-context requests. Immediate mitigations applied on 10/15: reduced max_batch_tokens for priority lane, bumped TTL for repeated keys to 30m, and routed long-context requests to an isolated worker pool. Result: p95 down 20–25%, 503s dropped significantly.

Customer impact: intermittent user-facing failures in claims ingestion and triage workflows for ~90 minutes (rolling degradation). Clearwave has requested an explanation and a commercial concession.

Recommended leadership asks:
- Approve a one-time service credit equal to 10% of October billed usage for Clearwave (conservative, avoids protracted negotiation).
- Approve a short-term Dedicated capacity trial (30 days, no charge) for their priority lane to prove stability while we harden routing and prefetch behavior.
- Fast-track INF-1429 follow-ups: permanent per-tenant soft-prefetch, per-tenant batch limits, and improved TTL autosuggestions in Optimize.

I'll prep a 1-page customer-facing summary for Aisha and a 3-slide exec note for Sales + CS. Please let me know approval or edits; timebox for a decision by EOD tomorrow (10/17).

Thanks —Rachel
Rachel Kim
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
